channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: CoreWeave Shares Plunge as CEO Expresses Confidence
item.description: CoreWeave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company’s business model. Nick Turner has more on "The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Exporter Dollar Sales Bolster Malaysian Ringgit, Analysts Say
item.description: Malaysian exporters are likely increasing conversions of their foreign-currency earnings into the ringgit, which stands to boost the local exchange rate through the rest of the year, analysts say.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Wong

item.title: Anthropic Revenue Hits $16.8 Billion in Quarter Before IPO
item.description: Anthropic PBC told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, as the artificial intelligence company pushes ahead with plans to go public.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz, Natasha Mascarenhas, Rebecca Torrence and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: CreditSights Head of Strategy on Bond Market Volatility
item.description: Winnie Cisar, Global Head of Strategy at CreditSights, discusses the strain from heavy corporate borrowing, including debt tied to AI infrastructure. She said individual issuer problems such as CoreWeave’s may coexist with a broader surge in issuance that is challenging investors’ ability to absorb new debt. She speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Slide as Hot Inflation & AI Credit Fears Hit Markets
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Vanguard President & CIO Greg Davis, UBS Equity Research Analyst, Large-Cap Banks & Consumer Finance Erika Najarian, Janus Henderson CEO Ali Dibadj, CreditSights Global Head of Strategy Winnie Cisar, DoubleLine Global Sovereign & Emerging Markets Head Bill Campbell, Cisco Chair & CEO Chuck Robbins, Blackstone Global Head of Digital Infrastructure Mike Forman, Nuveen Global Head of Infrastructure Jessica Bailey, KKR Head of North American Infrastructure Brandon Freiman, Loop Capital Founder, Chairman & CEO Jim Reynolds, & Huel CEO James McMaster. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CAIS Summit Panel on AI Buildout
item.description: At a forum in Beverly Hills, the discussion focused on obstacles to expanding AI data centers, including rising energy costs and weakening public support for construction. Blackstone’s Mike Forman said infrastructure supply constraints are worsening, particularly around power: utilities that once could connect projects within six to twelve months may now quote waits of up to seven years, require investments as high as $1 billion, and offer less certainty. The panel of Mike Forman, Jessica Bailey & Brandon Freiman speak to Romaine Bostick at the CAIS Summit Panel. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Janus Henderson CEO on Going Private, M&A Deals
item.description: Janus Henderson CEO Ali Dibadj said the firm is energized by its move to private ownership and is using the flexibility to invest in people, technology including AI, new products and client service. He said quarterly earnings pressures had constrained those investments, despite the firm’s growth as a public company. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia, Anthropic Weigh In On AI Safeguards
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he would halt the supply of chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software, though he doesn’t believe that the current level of concern about the technology is warranted. AI executives such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have proposed an industrywide slowdown to address the concerns. Meantime, Anthropic held an investor day Wednesday as it advances plans for a potential IPO at an approximately $2 trillion valuation, amid growing concerns about AI safety and threats. We get reaction from Bloomberg Tech host Ed Ludlow & Jacqueline Corbelli, Co-Founder and CEO at Brightline Partners. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vanguard CIO Greg Davis on Market, Inflation Outlook
item.description: Vanguard President and CIO Greg Davis said the CPI report was one data point for markets and the Federal Reserve to assess, while noting inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target and the Fed still has work to do. Davis said Vanguard generally expects one to two rate hikes over the coming months, depending on incoming data. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tesla-SpaceX Deal News Possible This Year, Barclays Analyst Says
item.description: A merger between Elon Musk’s Tesla Inc. and SpaceX could be announced ahead of the electric-vehicle maker’s annual general meeting, according to analysts at Barclays.
item.dc:creator: Peyton Forte

item.title: Rocket Lab Falls After Neutron Rocket Debut Delayed to 2027
item.description: Rocket Lab Corp. again delayed the debut of its new, more powerful Neutron rocket, pushing the vehicle’s first flight to 2027.
item.dc:creator: Loren Grush

item.title: Apple to Release AI Platform in Mainland China
item.description: Apple is planning to launch Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December. This is a huge market for the company. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman broke the news and has more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nuclear Startup Kairos Raises $643 Million for Tennessee Project
item.description: Kairos Power LLC, a nuclear-energy startup, lined up $643 million in private and government funding to support construction of its demonstration reactor in Tennessee.
item.dc:creator: Will Wade

item.title: Apple Prepares to Debut First AI Features in China in December
item.description: Apple Inc. is gearing up to release its artificial intelligence platform in mainland China, following a lengthy regulatory delay that has kept the company’s AI features out of one of its most important markets.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Nvidia's Huang Says He Would Not Sell Chips to Irresponsible AI Customers
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang says his company would stop selling chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software. He talks extensively about AI safety and how the industry is growing with Bloomberg's Emily Chang in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Says Market Acting ‘Irrationally,’ Stands by Model
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator, facing a plunge in the company’s stock and bond prices, said the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company’s business model.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Nvidia CEO Says He Would Cut Off Buyers Who Build Unsafe AI
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said he would halt the supply of chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software, though he doesn’t believe that the current level of concern about the technology is warranted.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Uruguay Hails $5.7 Billion Project in Solar Plant, Data Centers
item.description: Uruguay President Yamandu Orsi unveiled plans for $5.7 billion in data centers and solar power, touting them as the largest private investment in the South American nation’s history.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Gualtieri and Ken Parks

item.title: Chip Stocks Erase $1 Trillion in Value as Rout Deepens
item.description: A closely watched gauge of semiconductor stocks erased $1.6 trillion in market value in a six-day losing streak as concerns mount over higher interest rates, stretched valuations and the enormous cost of building artificial-intelligence infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Subrat Patnaik

item.title: OpenAI Vows Not to Use Trade Secrets Allegedly Taken From Apple
item.description: OpenAI agreed not to use trade secrets that Apple Inc. claims were stolen by employees who defected from the iPhone maker to the artificial intelligence startup while a legal fight between the companies plays out.
item.dc:creator: Annelise Levy (Bloomberg Law), Mark Gurman and Georgia Fearn
